bank.question: Countries that drive on the left
bank.answer: Which side of the road they drive on — gold drives on the left
bank.notes: About 75 countries and territories drive on the left — roughly a third of the world’s people. Mostly the old British Empire, plus Japan, Thailand, Indonesia and Mozambique. Source: Wikipedia, Left- and right-hand traffic.

bank.question: How corrupt every country is — Corruption Perceptions Index 2025
bank.answer: Corruption — Transparency International’s Corruption Perceptions Index
bank.notes: Transparency International, CPI 2025 (published February 2026): 182 countries scored from 0 (highly corrupt) to 100 (very clean). Cleanest: Denmark, 89. Bottom: Somalia and South Sudan, 9. Grey = not scored.

bank.question: The year women won the vote, on equal terms with men
bank.answer: When women got the vote — the year each country gave women the same voting rights as men
bank.notes: Equal terms with men. Several let some women vote earlier: the UK in 1918 (over-30s only), Norway in 1907 (with a property limit), Portugal in 1931 (educated women only). Switzerland waited until 1971 — and its last canton, Appenzell Innerrhoden, until 1990. The Vatican holds no elections for anyone. Source: Wikipedia, Women’s suffrage.

bank.question: Everywhere the Vikings reached
bank.answer: The Vikings — how far they sailed, raided and traded from Scandinavia
bank.notes: c. 793–1110. West to Newfoundland (L’Anse aux Meadows — tree rings date the wood cutting to exactly 1021), east down the Russian rivers to Constantinople, Baghdad and the Caspian. Lindisfarne 793, Seville 844, Paris 845. Jerusalem: King Sigurd the Crusader, 1110.

bank.question: Every country that still has a king, queen or emperor
bank.answer: Monarchies — gold have their own monarch, purple share King Charles III
bank.notes: 43 monarchies. 28 have their own (Japan’s emperor, Saudi Arabia, Spain, Thailand, Morocco…), and 15 Commonwealth realms share King Charles III — the UK, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Jamaica and more. The Vatican counts: the Pope is an elected absolute monarch. Source: Wikipedia, List of current monarchies.

bank.question: Every landlocked country
bank.answer: Landlocked countries — no coastline at all
bank.notes: 44 UN countries plus Kosovo have no sea coast. Only two are doubly landlocked — surrounded entirely by other landlocked countries: Liechtenstein and Uzbekistan. Kazakhstan is the biggest; the Caspian is a lake. Bolivia lost its coast to Chile in the War of the Pacific (1879–84) and still has a navy.

bank.question: Every country that has hosted the Summer Olympics
bank.notes: 19 countries, Athens 1896 to Paris 2024. The USA leads with four (St Louis 1904, LA 1932 and 1984, Atlanta 1996) — LA 2028 makes five. Britain and France have three each. Russia is shaded for Moscow 1980 (USSR). Africa has never hosted.

bank.question: Every country that has won the World Cup
bank.answer: FIFA World Cup winners — with how many times each has won it
bank.notes: Only eight nations have ever won it. Brazil 5 (1958, 62, 70, 94, 2002) · Germany 4 (1954, 74 and 90 as West Germany, 2014) · Italy 4 (1934, 38, 82, 2006) · Argentina 3 (1978, 86, 2022) · France 2 (1998, 2018) · Uruguay 2 (1930, 50) · Spain 2 (2010, and 2026 — 1–0 over Argentina after extra time) · England 1 (1966, shaded here on the whole UK). Source: FIFA.

bank.question: Every country that borders only one other country
bank.answer: Countries with exactly one neighbour by land
bank.notes: Portugal (Spain), Ireland and the UK (each other), South Korea (North Korea), Haiti and the Dominican Republic (each other), Qatar (Saudi Arabia), Brunei (Malaysia), Timor-Leste and Papua New Guinea (Indonesia), Gambia (Senegal), Lesotho (South Africa), Monaco (France), San Marino and the Vatican (Italy) — and Bahrain, whose only border is a checkpoint on an artificial island in the middle of the King Fahd Causeway. Canada and Denmark were on this list until June 2022, when they split Hans Island in the Arctic down the middle and gained a 1.3 km land border with each other. Source: Wikipedia, List of countries and territories by number of land borders.

bank.question: How many time zones every country spans
bank.answer: Time zones — how many each country spans, overseas territories included (shaded with their country)
bank.notes: France has the most: 12, thanks to its overseas territories from Polynesia to the Indian Ocean (13 counting its Antarctic claim). Then Russia and the USA 11, Australia and the UK 9, Canada and New Zealand 5, Brazil, Denmark (with Greenland) and Mexico 4. China, nearly as wide as the USA, uses just one. Source: Wikipedia, List of time zones by country.

bank.question: Every country’s all-time Summer Olympic medal count
bank.answer: All-time Summer Olympic medals — every country shaded by its total, numbers on the 11 with 500 or more
bank.notes: Through Paris 2024: USA 2,774 · Russia 1,623 · Germany 1,418 · Great Britain 986 · France 824 · China 727 · Italy 658 · Australia 594 · Japan 542 · Hungary 530 · Sweden 514. Russia includes the Soviet Union, the Russian Empire, the 1992 Unified Team and the ROC; Germany includes East and West Germany. Other defunct teams — Czechoslovakia, Yugoslavia and the like — are not credited to today’s countries. 140 countries on the map have won at least one. Source: Wikipedia, All-time Olympic Games medal table.

bank.question: Every country with nuclear weapons
bank.notes: Nine: the USA, Russia, the UK, France, China, India, Pakistan, North Korea — and Israel, which has never confirmed it. Russia and the USA hold around 90% of all warheads. South Africa built six bombs and dismantled them. Source: SIPRI Yearbook 2025.

bank.question: The G7 and the rest of the G20
bank.answer: The G20 — gold is the G7, purple the rest of the G20
bank.notes: The G20 is 19 countries plus the European Union and, since 2023, the African Union. The G7 inner circle: the US, Canada, the UK, France, Germany, Italy and Japan. Russia was in the G8 until it was suspended in 2014.

bank.question: Every country that uses the euro
bank.answer: The euro — every country that uses it, in the EU or not
bank.notes: 21 EU members use the euro — Bulgaria joined on 1 January 2026. Six more use it without being in the EU: Andorra, Monaco, San Marino and the Vatican by agreement, Montenegro and Kosovo on their own. Denmark has a legal opt-out.

bank.question: The countries that stayed neutral in World War II
bank.answer: WWII neutrals — gold stayed out the whole war, orange only joined the Allies at the very end
bank.notes: Ireland (which called the war “The Emergency”), Portugal, Spain, Switzerland and Sweden, plus Andorra, Liechtenstein and the Vatican, stayed out. Neutral Spain still sent the “Blue Division” of volunteers to fight for Germany on the Eastern Front. San Marino was bombed by the RAF in June 1944 and declared war on Germany that September; Turkey declared war in February 1945 — the price of a seat at the founding of the UN. Denmark, Norway, the Netherlands, Belgium, Luxembourg and Iceland were neutral too, until they were invaded. Source: Wikipedia, Neutral powers during World War II.

bank.question: The Schengen Area — Europe without border checks
bank.notes: 29 members: 25 EU countries plus Iceland, Norway, Switzerland and Liechtenstein. Romania and Bulgaria became full members on 1 January 2025. Ireland opted out and Cyprus hasn’t joined. Monaco, San Marino and the Vatican are open de facto. Named after a village in Luxembourg.

bank.question: The New Seven Wonders of the World
bank.answer: The New Seven Wonders of the World
bank.notes: Picked in a 2007 worldwide public vote run by the New7Wonders Foundation. The Great Pyramid of Giza, the last survivor of the ancient seven, was given honorary status rather than a place on the list.

bank.question: The Seven Summits — the highest mountain on each continent
bank.answer: The Seven Summits — the highest peak on every continent
bank.notes: Everest 8,849 m · Aconcagua 6,961 m · Denali 6,190 m · Kilimanjaro 5,895 m · Elbrus 5,642 m · Vinson 4,892 m · Puncak Jaya 4,884 m. Some lists use Australia’s Kosciuszko (2,228 m) instead of Puncak Jaya.

bank.question: The 16 host cities of the 2026 World Cup
bank.answer: The 2026 FIFA World Cup host cities
bank.notes: 11 in the USA, 3 in Mexico, 2 in Canada — 48 teams and 104 matches, 11 June to 19 July 2026. The opener was at Mexico City’s Estadio Azteca, the first stadium to host games at three World Cups; the final at MetLife Stadium, New York New Jersey, where Spain beat Argentina 1–0 after extra time.

bank.question: Every country whose name ends in -stan
bank.notes: Seven: Afghanistan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Pakistan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan. "-stan" is Persian for "land of": Afghanistan is the land of the Afghans. Source: Wikipedia, -stan.

bank.question: Every country where French is an official language
bank.answer: Countries where French is an official language
bank.notes: 26 countries: France, Belgium, Switzerland, Luxembourg, Monaco, Canada, Haiti and Vanuatu, and in Africa Benin, Burundi, Cameroon, the Central African Republic, Chad, Comoros, the Republic of the Congo, DR Congo, Côte d’Ivoire, Djibouti, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, Guinea, Madagascar, Rwanda, Senegal, Seychelles and Togo. Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger dropped it as an official language in 2023–25. Lebanon is not one: Arabic is its only official language. Source: Wikipedia, list of countries where French is an official language.

bank.question: Every country that borders Russia
bank.answer: Countries with a land border with Russia
bank.notes: Fourteen: Norway, Finland, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania and Poland (those two through Kaliningrad), Belarus, Ukraine, Georgia, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, China, Mongolia and North Korea. The USA and Japan are across the sea. Source: Wikipedia, Borders of Russia.

bank.question: Every country with more than 100 million people
bank.answer: Countries with more than 100 million people
bank.notes: Sixteen: India, China, the USA, Indonesia, Pakistan, Nigeria, Brazil, Bangladesh, Russia, Mexico, Ethiopia, Japan, the Philippines, Egypt, DR Congo and Vietnam (the newest, in 2023). Next in line: Iran, about 91 million, and Turkey, about 87 million. Japan is shrinking but still has about 124 million. Source: UN World Population Prospects 2024.

bank.question: Every member of the Arab League
bank.notes: 22 members, from Mauritania to Oman: Algeria, Bahrain, Comoros, Djibouti, Egypt, Iraq, Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, Libya, Mauritania, Morocco, Oman, Palestine, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Somalia, Sudan, Syria, Tunisia, the UAE and Yemen. Lebanon was a founder in 1945; Syria, suspended in 2011, was readmitted in 2023. Source: Wikipedia, Arab League.

bank.question: Every country with "Guinea" in its name
bank.notes: Four: Guinea, Guinea-Bissau and Equatorial Guinea in West Africa, and Papua New Guinea on the other side of the world. A Spanish explorer, Yñigo Ortiz de Retez, named New Guinea in 1545: he thought its people looked like those of Africa’s Guinea coast. Source: WorldAtlas.

bank.question: Every country that has played in a men’s World Cup final
bank.answer: Countries that have played in a World Cup final — gold won at least one
bank.notes: Thirteen nations, 23 finals, 1930 to 2026. Won at least one (gold): Germany (8 finals, six as West Germany), Brazil (7), Argentina (7), Italy (6), France (4), Uruguay (2), Spain (2) and England (1, shaded on the whole UK). Reached a final but never won (purple): the Netherlands (3), Hungary (2), Czechoslovakia (2, in 1934 and 1962, shaded on Czechia and Slovakia), Sweden (1) and Croatia (1). 1950 had no final as such: the Uruguay v Brazil decider of the final group counts. Source: Wikipedia, List of FIFA World Cup finals.

bank.question: Beirut–Rafic Hariri International Airport
bank.notes: Arabic and English side by side, and seven of the eight flights are ME, Middle East Airlines, whose home is Beirut (EY is Etihad). The destinations are MEA's network (Paris, London, Rome, Frankfurt, Dubai, Istanbul, Athens) and Beirut is the one city missing. Every flight number and time is real: it is the airport's own departure list for 22 October 2026.

bank.notes: A Spanish board where most flights are IB, Iberia, Spain's flag carrier. Barcelona is on the board, so it is not Barcelona; the long-haul flights to Bogotá and New York point to Iberia's hub. Madrid is missing.

bank.notes: Portuguese words (Embarque, Última chamada, Atrasado) and TP, TAP Air Portugal, on almost every flight. Porto and Funchal are on the board, so it is Portugal's other big airport; Luanda and São Paulo are TAP's Lusophone long-haul routes from its hub.

bank.question: Athens International Airport
bank.notes: The Greek alphabet and A3, Aegean Airlines, on seven of the eight flights. Thessaloniki and Heraklion are on the board, so it is not those; Aegean's hub is Athens, the city missing.

bank.question: Istanbul Airport
bank.notes: Turkish words (Zamanında = on time, Gecikmeli = delayed, İptal = cancelled) and TK, Turkish Airlines, on almost every flight. Ankara, İzmir and Antalya are listed, so it is the one big Turkish city missing: Istanbul, TK's hub.

bank.question: Amsterdam Airport Schiphol
bank.notes: Dutch words (Vertrek, Op tijd, Vertraagd, Geannuleerd) and KL, KLM, on most flights, plus HV (Transavia's Dutch arm). Curaçao is a Dutch Caribbean island, a classic KLM route from its only hub.

bank.question: Dubai International Airport
bank.notes: Arabic and English, and the airline is EK, Emirates, on seven flights (FZ is flydubai). Emirates has a single hub, Dubai, and the destinations span every continent, as a giant hub's would.

bank.question: Frankfurt Airport
bank.notes: German words (Abflug, Pünktlich, Verspätet, Annulliert) and German city names (Rom, München, Laibach = Ljubljana), so a German-speaking airport. LH, Lufthansa, has two hubs, Frankfurt and Munich, and München is on the board, so it must be Frankfurt. DE is Condor, also based in Frankfurt.

bank.question: Munich Airport
bank.notes: German board, Lufthansa everywhere, so one of its two hubs. Frankfurt is on the board, so this is the other one: Munich. Hamburg, Berlin and Köln are listed too, which rules them out.

bank.question: Zurich Airport
bank.notes: German again, but the airline is LX, Swiss (and WK, Edelweiss), not Lufthansa, so Switzerland. Genf (Geneva) is on the board, which leaves Swiss's hub, Zurich.

bank.question: Brussels Airport
bank.notes: Every word in French AND Dutch, which only Belgium does. SN is Brussels Airlines, and Kinshasa is its trademark route to the former Belgian Congo.

bank.question: In which decade did the Michelin Guide award its first stars?
bank.notes: Single stars from 1926; the three-star scale came in 1931. The guide itself dates from 1900.

bank.question: Bluetooth is named after a 10th-century king who united his country's tribes into one kingdom. Which country?
bank.notes: King Harald 'Bluetooth' Gormsson united the Danish tribes. The logo joins his initials, H and B, in runes.

bank.question: What was the first animal sent into space?
bank.notes: In 1947, on a captured German V-2 rocket fired from New Mexico, to see what radiation would do to living things. They came back alive.
